title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description:
Two singly linked chains, list1 and list2, each contain values in nondecreasing order. Return the head of one chain containing every node from both inputs in nondecreasing order. Preserve duplicates: equal values from different chains each appear in the result.

Either input can be empty, in which case the other chain is already the required answer. Both can be empty as well: return a null head (serialized as null). No requirement distinguishes equal-valued nodes by origin; the returned value sequence is the contract. Do not append an extra sentinel node to the returned chain.

The useful observation is that the least unmerged element must be one of the two current heads. Selecting that node, advancing its source, and repeating avoids sorting everything from scratch. Once one chain runs out, the other already has the correct internal order.

Example 1:

Input: list1 = [1,2,4], list2 = [1,3,4]
Output: [1,1,2,3,4,4]

Example 2:

Input: list1 = [], list2 = []
Output: null

Example 3:

Input: list1 = [], list2 = [0]
Output: [0]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= length of each chain <= 5,000.
  • -10,000 <= node.val <= 10,000.
  • Each input chain is sorted in nondecreasing order.
